summary: A 1902 range light at Beacon Hill, built to guide ships over the bar into St. Joseph Bay; a modern tower replaced it in 1955.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record and the archive give 1902 for the station's establishment and the original lens installation (USLHS 'Year Original Lens Installed: 1902'). LighthouseFriends says the lens lantern was displayed from August 1902 and the third-order lens was lit in March 1903. The story says the station went into service in 1902 (Florida Lighthouse Association) and gives both lens dates, with their sources.

The archive gives 1960 (USLHS 'Year Discontinued: 1960'). The Florida Lighthouse Association and LighthouseFriends say a modern 78-foot iron tower replaced the light in 1955; LighthouseFriends says the dwelling was sold in 1960. The story gives both dates and says which source gives which.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster (5 lines) is the USLHS archive's, from NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory; the archive is the only roster source. LighthouseFriends agrees on Lupton 1902-1928 and Brooks 1928-1938 and gives Roberts as Walter A. Roberts, Jr. The archive prints Minnie I. Lupton as two laborer stints (1903-1922, 1922-1926); LighthouseFriends gives 1903-1926 as one span. The 1900 and 1901 Board entries cite the scan page the corpus printed; printed page numbers were not read. No OCR table was matched by column position. The Light-House Board's 1902 report and later reports are not in the local corpus (the lhb series ends with fiscal 1901), so the 1902 description, the 1921 Curlew grounding, the World War II watch, the 1955/1960/1979 history and the 2018 storm are cited to LighthouseFriends and the Florida Lighthouse Association, both secondary. The Coast Guard Historian's page for the rear range light could not be read: the archived copy returned 403, and the raw capture came back compressed. The Pensacola Journal page (9 April 1909) that the 'St. Joseph Point' and 'Lupton' search returned was not read and is not used. Record items with no source located: the front range 'lost' status, the tower 'wood_frame 12.0 m lost' entry, and the 'focal height 24.4 m' value. The record's 1960 deactivation date is kept as the archive's; the 1955 replacement is kept as LighthouseFriends and the Florida Lighthouse Association give it. The private owner of the dwelling and the children who died are not named in the story. No photos are proposed.
